current_bottleneck: 293b-v0 improved the new reset line from 3/11 to 4/11 by helping calibration and cointegration, but it did not improve the actual path-shape failures. The active issue is now narrower: the family can learn local stochastic law and some global window dependence, but it still lacks a mechanism that controls long-horizon path shape, especially mean reversion, level-law fidelity, regime-sensitive width allocation, and pathwise jump ordering.
last_result_summary: Iteration 130 implemented, trained, and evaluated 293b-v0, adding one global path latent to the 293a fixed-horizon joint-token family. It scored 4/11, passing surface, block_ar, cointegration, and cross_cell_correlation. Relative to 293a it improved calibration and recovered cointegration, but level KS stayed at 2/25 and MR worsened from 0.082 to 0.034, showing that the added latent acted more like extra entropy/context than a true path-shape controller.
next_step_recommendation: Do post-experiment analysis comparing 293a vs 293b before adding another mechanism. The next move should target path-shape coupling rather than more generic latent capacity.
current_best_model: 277d-v0, 279a-v0, 281a-v0, 281b-v0, and 282b-v0 are the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11 in the two-level reset.
current_best_note: 282b is still the cleanest current Stage B objective frontier at 5/11, but 284b and 285a strengthen the conclusion that the real cap is now the Stage A support object rather than the Stage B weighting law.
